metadata.title: Human Superintelligence Readiness Index (HSRI): Repository Snapshot v0.3.0-dev
metadata.description:
HSRI v0.3.0-dev: Exploratory Research Prototype

This deposit provides an archival snapshot of the Human Superintelligence Readiness Index (HSRI) repository at milestone v0.3.0-dev. HSRI is an exploratory, non-psychometrically-validated proxy benchmark designed to evaluate national-level cognitive, institutional, and infrastructure preparedness under advancing artificial intelligence. The composite framework harmonizes 780 national observations across 39 nations structured into four equal-weighted pillars (25% each): Foundational Cognitive Infrastructure, Technological Fluency, Epistemic Rigor, and Critical Discernment.

Epistemic and Governance Disclaimer (Rule 12): This release represents an exploratory research prototype. Behavioral experiment batteries (EXP-01, EXP-02, EXP-03) represent stimulus development only; synthetic-persona pilots test stimulus behavior only and provide no empirical evidence regarding human cognition. Stimuli are cleared for IRB submission. Not validated on human participants. Structural missingness is explicitly preserved without naive imputation (e.g. non-EU EMLI missingness, non-participating PIAAC PSTRE economies), and 86 unrated nations are excluded without score extrapolation.

metadata.title: HSRI Multi-Model Divergence Log Dataset v0.1
metadata.description:
HSRI Multi-Model Divergence Log Dataset (v0.1)

This dataset contains the structured deliberative audit logs generated by the HSRI multi-agent governance pipeline. Methodological propositions (pillar weighting, structural missingness, macro-exposure gap modeling) are debated by autonomous AI agents representing proponent and skeptic stances across five review board lanes (Psychometrics, Cross-Cultural Methods, Geopolitics, Governance & Ethics, and Technical Architecture).

Epistemic and Governance Disclaimer: All live multi-model debates to date have executed solely against the Google Gemini 3.8 Flash model family due to environment key provisioning constraints; other model evaluations are logged as SKIPPED. Results represent single-model-family deliberative behavior rather than cross-family consensus. Logged conservative default entries represent human governance decisions rather than empirical model output. The dataset is provided as an open research resource for AI governance and multi-agent alignment studies.
